key_insight: Coarsening-based GNN training can lose critical information on heterophilic graphs, and ACE fixes this by reconstructing discarded content with adaptive complementary enhancement.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical plug-and-play way to scale GNN training to large graphs without sacrificing accuracy in heterophilic settings.
method: Learn a projector to reconstruct original node features from the coarsened graph.
Use anisotropic structural regularization to preserve local heterophily in the learned representation.
Balance coarsened-graph training and full-graph auxiliary training with homoscedastic uncertainty weighting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing consistent gains on heterophilic benchmarks while keeping competitive performance on homophilic graphs with minimal overhead.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of feature reconstruction and the added auxiliary objectives may introduce extra tuning complexity.
paper_title: Remedying Coarsening-Based GNN Training under Heterophily via Adaptive Complementary Enhancement
